source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 8 'INCOME NOT TAXABLE FOR PA PIT PURPOSES' first bullet; the PA-40 has no Social Security line; PDF page 11 'Eligible Employer-Sponsored Retirement Plans'; PDF page 12 Distributions item 1; PDF pages 12-13 Code 1 & 2 and Code 7; PDF page 8 list; PDF page 15 Line 3

worked: Only taxable Social Security is in AGI, and it comes out in full; the pension is out too, so only the dividends are taxed. Federal AGI = private pension person 0 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security 34,000.00 + dividends 20,000.00 = 104,000.00. Taxable Social Security is the federal worksheet's result on the gross benefit and other income. Federal taxable income = 104,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 + age 65 addition 3,200.00 = 69,300.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 104,000.00; less 50,000.00 private pension person 0 (pa_employer_plans); less 34,000.00 taxable Social Security (social_security exempt; gross 40,000.00; no PA line); income after reliefs = 20,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 20,000.00. Tax = 20,000.00 x 0.0307 = 614.00. No credit in the projection; state income tax 614.00. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 20,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 20,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 20,000.00; Line 12 614.00. Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 20,000.00 is over 15,250.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
